Table 8.1 shows some data relating to the properties of air, gel and body tissue. The data are given to three significant figures.

Table 8.1

material | density / $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ | speed of sound / $\text{m s}^{-1}$ | specific acoustic impedance / $\text{kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$
air |  | 340 | 440
gel | 1200 | 1400 | 
tissue | 1090 |  | $1.68 \times 10^{6}$
parts.text: Show that the specific acoustic impedance of gel is $1.68 \times 10^{6}\text{ kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Complete Table 8.1 by calculating the missing values to three significant figures. Use the space below for any working that you need.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: Use the information in (a) to calculate the intensity reflection coefficient for:

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Use your answers in (b) to explain why gel is applied to the skin during ultrasound scanning.
